narration.text: Double light speed, and atoms change.
It's not just faster internet. Chemistry itself shifts.
Light is fixed at exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.
A number called the fine-structure constant is about 1/137.
It shrinks when light gets faster, and it governs how atoms bond.
Double light speed, and it halves.
Some theories say life needs it between 1/180 and 1/85.
Halved, it falls outside that window, so the answer is chemistry, not speed.
